To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the long-term treatment of rats with hydralazines leads to the lowering of retinol level, to the lowering of activity of superoxide-dismutase and, consequently, to an increase of free radical activity reflected by the enhancement of lipid peroxidative processes.
the long-term use of hydralazines causes the lowering of retinol level.

the long term use of hydralazines in rats caused the decrease in the retinol levels in the serum and the liver, which is reflected by the increased lipid peroxidations and decreased activity of superoxide dimutase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of using retinol in the prophylaxis of late toxicity of the drug.
the possibility of retinol use in the prevention of the development of hydralazin-induced collagenosis-like syndrome.
the role of retinol in the development of the hydralazine-induced collagenosis syndrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
retinol is a factor limiting free radical damage and the development of collagenosis-like syndrome in rats treated solely or together with hydrazine.
the long-term use of hydralazin causes the lowering of the level of retinol and superoxide dismutases activity.
the long-term hydralazine administration caused a decrease in the retinol serum and liver levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
retinol is a protective agent in the case of hydralazin-induced collagenosis.
retinol supplementation in rats treated with hydrazine limited the lowering of the serum and hepatic retinol level.
the retinol administration to rats treated solely with the hydralazine limited the lowering of the serum and liver retinol concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
retinol supplementation in rats treated with hydrazine limits the development of late toxicity of the drug.
the retinol supplementation in rats treated with hydrazine limits the development of free radical activity and lipid peroxidation processes.
retinol supplementation can prevent the development of hydralazin-induced collagenosis in rats.
